description: The tsl acquire path landed in 8141f91 (EndfLibrary::thermal_url, well_known_tsl, EndfCache::fetch_tsl/fetch_tsl_by_name/download_tsl_tape). Remaining: make the LIVE thermal tests use it so they download portably instead of soft-skipping on a hardcoded path. Targets: outram-mc pincell.rs (op-6tz.12, tsl-HinH2O) and njoy thermal_graphite_coherent.rs (graphite MAT 30/31/32). notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
PARTIALLY CLOSED 2026-08-14, and the route changed. NOT closing -- one of the two targets is now blocked on a different, identified bead.

ROUTE CHANGE. This bead proposed un-gating the LIVE thermal tests by wiring them to EndfCache::fetch_tsl (network download). The embedded LEAPR decks added 2026-08-14 are a strictly better route for the same goal: no network, no cache, no IAEA availability question (that host is policy-blocked 403 from this environment, which is why this bead was marked 'NOT verifiable on this host'), and it works offline and in CI.

TARGET 1 -- GRAPHITE: DONE. tests/htr10_graphite_thermal_scattering_pebble_bed.rs and the new tests/triso_shell_thermal_scattering.rs both regenerate the graphite MF=7 law from the embedded tsl-crystalline-graphite deck via leapr::generate::generate_tape. No , no skip path, runs unconditionally. Verified: elastic 4.55555 b + inelastic 0.48162 b at 0.0253 eV, reproducing the 5.0378 b recorded under op-nhoa against the official ENDF/B-VIII.0 TAPE -- so the regenerate-from-deck path agrees with the tape path.

TARGET 2 -- outram-mc pincell.rs (tsl-HinH2O): STILL GATED, root cause identified and it is NOT this bead's to fix. The fallback is wired (locate_tsl_hinh2o now tries env var -> local path -> regenerate-from-embedded-deck), but regeneration FAILS for light water with NotPorted. Measured cause, from LeaprDeck::unsupported_features():
    'nss = 1 (secondary-scatterer mixed-moderator merge is not ported)'
tsl-HinH2O.leapr carries a SECONDARY SCATTERER -- the oxygen in the water molecule -- so producing its law needs the mixed-moderator merge, which this workspace's LEAPR port does not implement. That work is op-b2k (LEAPR copys/skold + run() driver + mixed-moderator merge). Graphite needs no secondary scatterer, which is why it regenerates and water does not.

The fallback is kept wired on purpose: it costs nothing when it fails, and the day op-b2k lands the pincell test un-gates ITSELF with no edit to this file. Adding op-b2k as a dependency to reflect that.

Also folded out a drift risk while in there: the S(alpha,beta) build temperature is now a single TSL_TEMPERATURE_K const shared by the regeneration call and ThermalScattering::from_endf_file, instead of two 293.6 literals.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
RESOLVED 2026-08-14 and verified. The thermal pincell is no longer data-gated.

The blocker recorded in the previous comment (nss = 1 secondary scatterer, op-b2k) was ported the same day by commit 9591944fb9 from a concurrent session. The regenerate-from-embedded-deck fallback wired into locate_tsl_hinh2o then started working WITH NO CODE CHANGE -- 9591944fb9 did not touch pincell.rs. That was the design intent when the fallback was committed while it could not yet succeed.

VERIFIED on this environment, no local tape, OUTRAM_TSL_HINH2O unset:
  [thermal pincell] S(alpha,beta) + nuclide build: 4.03s
  [thermal pincell] k_inf = 1.41053 +/- 0.00689  (npart=600, 40+60 gen, 8.1s)
Previously printed SKIP and asserted nothing.

Supporting gates: njoy leapr_h2o_secondary_scatterer 5 passed / 0 failed; outram-mc light_water_thermal_scattering 5 passed / 0 failed; outram-mc --lib --tests 274 passed / 0 failed.

Also confirmed the generate_tape change in 9591944fb9 (which added the trans and discre stages, GENERATOR_REVISION 1 -> 2) does NOT perturb the graphite numbers recorded under op-hc2o and op-6tz.35.1 -- C-in-graphite elastic still 4.55555 b and dominant, SiC elastic still exactly 0.0, both assertions still green. Consistent with that commit's claim that graphite cannot see the fix (twt = 0, no oscillators).

The stale doc comment on locate_tsl_hinh2o asserting the blocker is corrected in a2802a350b.

BOTH TARGETS NOW DONE: graphite (via htr10_graphite_thermal_scattering_pebble_bed.rs and triso_shell_thermal_scattering.rs) and tsl-HinH2O (pincell.rs). Neither needs a network download, so EndfCache::fetch_tsl was never needed for this bead's goal. Closing.

GitHub issue #25 mirrors this and is closed with the same evidence.

description:
Umbrella for giving tampines::components real physical dimensions.

FINDING (2026-08-03, while designing the digital-twin widget library): only Pipe carries real geometry (diameter, length, inclination, roughness -- crates/tampines/src/components/pipe.rs:37-43). HeatExchanger (heat_exchanger.rs:20) and SteamGenerator (via heat_exchanger.area) carry a heat-TRANSFER Area only, which is not an envelope -- a compact plate HX and a large shell-and-tube can share an area. Pump, Turbine, Valve, Condenser and CoolingTower carry no dimensional data at all.

WHY THIS BLOCKS THE WIDGET LIBRARY: outram-park-digital-twin-engine renders 'visual process objects whose rendering derives directly from physics state'. Its crate CLAUDE.md forbids new physics in the engine, so any dimension a widget needs must be added HERE, in tampines.

THE TRAP TO AVOID: HemSteamCv::get_volume() is reachable from Turbine (turbine.inlet) and SteamGenerator (secondary_side), but it is the THERMODYNAMIC control volume -- caller-supplied, unvalidated, used only to convert intensive to extensive properties (get_mass() = volume / specific_volume). The codebase convention is a 1 m3 dummy (TampinesSteamTableCV::get_ref_vol() returns exactly 1.0 m3) and Turbine::new never sets or scales it. Sizing a widget on it would draw every turbine identically at 1 m3. It represents the fluid parcel, not the machine casing. Do NOT use it for visual size.

Each child bead adds an honest envelope/size to one component. Prefer explicit named dimensions (casing length/diameter, shell height, footprint) over a bare Volume where the shape matters to the drawing; a single nominal Volume is acceptable where a rough size correlation is all that is wanted.
title: tampines components: physical size/volume representation for visualization

description:
rayon-core does not build for wasm32-unknown-unknown at all — it needs OS threads, and fails with 'cannot find module or crate sys'. Five crates depend on it unconditionally:
  boon-lay, nee_soon, njoy-outram-park-fork, outram-mc-libs, raffles
(nee_soon and raffles inherit it transitively via njoy-outram-park-fork / outram-mc-libs.)

COPY THE EXISTING PRECEDENT, do not invent a new shape: outram-foam-basic-lib already passes the wasm check because its rayon sits behind an off-by-default 'parallel' Cargo feature (op-yvj.4.1 / GH #10), with ComputeBackend::CpuMulti degrading to Serial when the feature is off. Its compute.rs module header documents the reasoning. Same treatment here.

Note the deliberate asymmetry with Android: rayon IS Android-clean (pure Rust, no system component) and is correctly NOT target-gated for it. So the gate must be a FEATURE, not cfg(not(target_arch=wasm32)) — otherwise Termux loses multi-core for no reason. outram-foam-basic-lib's Cargo.toml comments already spell this out.

Acceptance: cargo check -p <each> --lib --target wasm32-unknown-unknown passes; native default build keeps rayon and is unchanged; cargo check --all-targets --target aarch64-linux-android still clean.
title: wasm class A: put rayon behind an off-by-default feature (5 crates)
